: Judgment :

The Special Land Acquisition Officer, KIADB, Bengaluru has sent this reference under Sections 30 and 31(2) of L.A. Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred as 'L.A. Act' for short) for apportionment of compensation amount.

.2. The brief facts of the case is that the land bearing Sy.No.14 measuring 1 acre 3 guntas of Hosakerehalli village, Uttarahalli Hobli Bengaluru South Taluka has been acquired for the purpose of Small Scale Industries.
Preliminary notification was issued on 31.03.2004.
The final notification was issued on 14.06.2006.
The award has been passed on 31.01.2012.
The possession has been taken on L.A.C. No.50/2012 18.11.2011.
The L.A.O. has fixed the compensation of Rs.21,50,000/-.
As O.S.No.2062/1990 has been pending, the L.A.O. has referred the matter to this Court and has deposited a sum of Rs.21,50,000/-.
The said amount has been kept in F.D. in Karnataka Bank, CMM Court branch, Bengaluru.
.3. After receipt of reference, this court issued notice to both parties.
The claimants 1 to 3 and 8 have entered appearance through their counsels.

The claimant No. 4 is shown to be abated, claimant No.
5 remained absent.
.4. Claimant No.1 Ammayyamma has filed claim statement stating that the petition as laid is not maintainable.

sentences.text: It is stated that 1 acre 3 guntas situated at Hosakerehalli village has been acquired as per the notification.
But the averment made by the petitioner as per Revenue records does not convey any meaning as there is no dispute about the ownership of the acquired lands.

The amount of compensation granted is inadequate; that the property is situated in prime locality and it has great potential value and the improvements, malkies, trees and bore well are not taken into consideration.
.6.
It is stated that the property was the separate property of late.

Narasimhaiah husband of claimant No. 1 and he had filed form No. 7 and the same was granted to him in LRF No. 4341 of 1975-76 as he was cultivating the same and all the revenue records stood in his name; that grant was personal to him and not in respect of any family.
Form No. 10 was granted to late Narasimhaiah on 16.05.1981 after complying L.A.C. No.50/2012 with all formalities.
Father of Narasimhaiah late.
Muniswamappa was working in Accounts General Office as a peon and was in government service and the family had no ancestral properties.
Narasimhaiah was a tenant and was agriculturist and he was granted the said land and he died on 03.01.1995 and subsequently the said land devolved on his heir that is Ammayyamma.
Narasimhaiah and his brothers were separate and each of the brothers had their own property and there was no joint family of any kind whatsoever.

As abundant caution Narasimhaiah and his brothers have entered into Family partition dated 31.03.1975 and the properties whichever items stood in the respective names of the respective brothers were taken and allotted to them and in any event, there was complete severance of status even prior thereto and there was no communion of interest of any kind as between late. Narasimhaiah and his brothers and sisters that is the other respondents.

In fact, in the suit O.S.No. 2062/90 the said family partition has already been marked as L.A.C. No.50/2012 Ex.D.1 and all the parties have admitted the same and have accepted the same and thus even under the said family partition the petition schedule land that is Sy.No. 14 of Hosakerehalli village has been shown as belonging to late. Narasimhaia and thus the alleged claim by the other respondents does not stand to reason.

It is stated that the entire compensation is to be paid to the title holders this respondent Ammayyamma whose land is notified for acquisition and in whose name the notice of acquisition and award is ordered and as such other respondents are not entitled to raise dispute.

Hence, prayed to release the entire amount to claimant No. 1.
.7.

The LRs of claimant No. 2 have filed claim statement stating that the present compensation awarded / solatium cannot be disbursed because, suit in O.S.No. 2062/1990 came to be partly decreed and appeal is preferred over the said judgment and decree in RFA No. 1391/2013.

The father of the present LRs has filed Cross Objections in RFA Cross Objections No. 33/2013 seeking setting aside the judgment and decree L.A.C. No.50/2012 passed in O.S.No. 2062/1990 dated 16.04.2013 and to award 9/40th share and for such other reliefs.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the claim petition.

.8. The claimant No. 8 Rajamma has filed claim statement stating that claimant No. 2 who is her youger brother i.e., Sri. G.V. Gopalaswamy has filed suit in O.S.No. 2062/1990, which is still pending before the City Civil Judge (CCH-2) at Bengaluru praying for partition and separate possession against all the children of late. M. Venkataswamappa and she has induct as defendant No. 7 and the claimant No. 1 is induct as LR of D-1(a) in the said suit.

5 Ammayyamma was managing the affairs of the joint family as a kartha and he was purchased /
acquired the same from and out of the joint family funds and after his death the said property was transferred in the name of his wife Ammayyamma i.e., claimant No. 1.

It is stated that her father late. M. L.A.C. No.50/2012 Venkataswamappa had acquired several properties through partition and all the properties which were acquired through partition is retained as joint family properties till date.
It is stated that husband of claimant No. 1 late. Narasimhaiah has sold some lands by making sites and has received large amount from various properties on behalf of the joint family.
The joint family was carrying on milk vending business since several decades and had very good income.

The late. Narasimhaiah i.e. husband of Ammayyamma has intentionally sold several joint family properties in- favour of his wife and his children and all the properties are subject matter of above said partition suit.

Hence, this claimant prayed not to disburse the compensation amount in-favour of claimant No. 1 i.e., Ammayyamma alone and as well as the said property is the subject matter (schedule item No. 4 in partition suit) of O.S.No. 2062/1990.
.9.
In order to prove their case, the General Power of Attorney holder of claimant No.1 has been examined L.A.C. No.50/2012 as PW.1.
The claimant No. 2(b) has been examined as PW.2.
The documents marked at Ex.P.1 to 19. .10.
Heard the arguments.

.11. The following points that would arise for my consideration are:
1) Which of the claimants are entitled to receive the compensation amount awarded to the acquired land deposited in this reference?
2. What order or award?
.12.

My findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1: As per decision Point No.2: As per final order, for the following:

is the General Power of Attorney.
.14. PW. 1 has stated that the acquired land was the separate property of late.
Narasimhaiah husband of L.A.C. No.50/2012 claimant No. 1 and his father.
He had filed form No. 7 and the same was granted to him in his personal capacity and LRF No. 4341 of 1975-76 as he was cultivating the same.
PW. 1 has stated that there was no joint family or family property or nucleus for acquisition.

Ex.P.14 is the form No.
10, which discloses that the grant has been made in-favour of Narasimhaiah to an extent of 4 acres 4 guntas in Sy.No. 14.
.15.

PW.1 has stated that his father died on 03.01.1995 and thereafter mutation has been made in the name of his mother i.e.,
claimant No.1.

are the nil Encumbrance certificate for the period from 01.06.1989 to 31.03.2004 and from 01.04.2004 to 06.09.2013 respectively.
.18. PW. 1 has stated that adjoining portion of same survey number to an extent of 1 acre 18 guntas was acquired for the purpose of formation of NICE road and compensation was granted to his mother.

He and his brother and sisters have no objection for releasing the entire compensation in the name of their mother claimant No. 1.
.19.

PW. 1 has stated that the present reference in-respect of portion of Sy.No. 14 of Hosakerehalli village in which respondent has acquired the land to an L.A.C. No.50/2012 extent of 1 acre 3 guntas which belongs to his mother.
She is entitled for entire compensation amount and they have all consented for the same.

.20. PW. 1 has stated that other claimants Gopal and others have filed objections before the respondent not to release the entire compensation to his mother alleging that they had instituted suit in O.S.No. 2062/1990 on the file of City Civil Court (CCH-2), Bengaluru for partition and separate possession of various properties including the present acquired property.
The present portion of the land bearing Sy.No. 14 which is item No. 4 in the plaint schedule.
PW. 1 has stated that the said suit has been dismissed.
Ex.P.2 is the judgment in O.S.No. 2062/1990.
From the judgment, it is seen that the defendant No. 1 in the said case is Narasimhaiah the husband of claimant No. 1 and the suit has been partly decreed.

It is held that the plaintiff is entitled to partition and separate possession of his 1/8th share in item No. 1 and 2 of schedule 'A' property, the ) Ammayyamma vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 15 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167841535/
7 defendants 1(a) to 1(j) L.A.C. No.50/2012 together entitled to 1/8th share and the defendants 3(a) to 3(d) are together entitled to 1/8th share and defendants 2, 4 and 7 are entitled to 1/8th share each in item No. 1 and 9 of the suit schedule 'A' property.

sentences.text: The suit of the plaintiff in-respect of suit schedule 'B' property is dismissed.

.21. From the judgment - Ex.P.2, it is seen that issue No. 2 is "whether the legal heirs of defendant No. 1 prove that item No. 2, 3, 4 and 12 of A schedule were self acquired properties of deceased defendant No. 1?.
The issue No. 2 is answered in the affirmative.

From the judgment, it is clear that item No. 4 of the suit A schedule property is self acquired property of Narasimhaiah.
.22.

PW.1 has stated that during life time of his father there was family settlement dated 31.03.1975 which was signed and executed by all the brothers, mother and one of sister of his father which is admitted by one and all in the said suit and it is marked as Ex.D.1 in the suit and the entire Sy.No. 14 of L.A.C. No.50/2012 Hosakerehalli village has been allotted to his father late.
Narasimhaiah under the said family partition and the acquired portion of land involved in this petition forms part of the same Sy.No. 14.
PW.1 has stated that other claimants have no right or share in the compensation amount and the claimant No. 1 is alone entitled to receive the compensation amount.
.23. During cross-examination he admits that the claimant No. 2 Gopalappa is his junior uncle.
Against the judgment in O.S.No. 2062/1990 (Ex.P.2) the claimant No. 2 has preferred an appeal.
He has stated that the said appeal is not still admitted.
He admits that the KIADB has passed consent award.
.24. The claimant No.2(b) Sanjay has been examined as PW.2.
He has stated that he is deposing for himself and on behalf of his mother B.N. Mangala and his sister Sahana who are legal heirs of deceased claimant No. 2, has been examined as PW.2.
He has stated that the compensation amount cannot be disbursed as suit in O.S.No. 2062/1990 has been partly L.A.C. No.50/2012 decreed and appeal is preferred in RFA No. No.1391/2013.
PW.2 has stated that their father filed Cross objections in RFA Cross objection No. 33/2013 seeking setting aside of the judgment and decree in O.S.No. 2062/1990 and to award 9/40 th share.

PW.2 has stated that RFA and Cross objections are heard and the matter is admitted; that unless the above RFA and Cross objections are disposed of, it will not be in the interest of parties to permit them to withdraw the amount claimed.

In support of his contention, he has produced certified copy of order sheet in RFA No.1391/2013 and connected cases as per Ex.P.19.
.25.
From the oral and documentary evidence, it is clear that Narasimhaiah has been granted the land by the Land Tribunal.
From the judgment in Ex.P.2, it is clear that the acquired property bearing Sy.No. 14 is self acquired property of Narasimhaiah.
The said Narasimhaiah died and his legal heirs have contended that the compensation amount can be paid to the claimant No. 1 Ammayyamma.
The RFA filed in-respect L.A.C. No.50/2012 of judgment in O.S.No. 2061/1990 has not been disposed of.
During the pendency of the case, Ammayyamma has expired.

Hence, I am of the view that LRs of claimant No. 1 are together entitled to receive the compensation amount,
however, this order is subject to the result of RFA No.1391/2013.
Accordingly point No.1 is answered partly in the affirmative.

O R DE R
The reference made by the respondent/SLAO, KIADB, Bengaluru under Sections 30 and 31(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 is hereby partly allowed.

LRs of Claimant No. 1 are entitled to receive the compensation amount in guntas of Hosakerehalli village, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluka with accrued interest thereon, subject to the result in RFA No.1391/2013 C/w RFA COB L.A.C.
No.50/2012 33/2013, which is pending on the file of the Hon'ble High Court.
The parties are at liberty to seek for modification of the order in terms of judgment in RFA No. 1391/2013 and connected case.
The above claimants shall have to execute indemnity bond with one surety,
undertaking to re-deposit the compensation amount either in this court or in any other court, if ordered to do so, which amount they are going to receive in this case.
The reference made by the respondent in-respect of claimant No. 2 is dismissed.
The reference made by the respondent in-respect of claimant No. 3 to 8 is rejected.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Judgment Writer, transcribed by her, revised by me and after corrections,
pronounced in open Court on this the 15th day of March, 2023.)
(Sheila B.M.), II Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge & Spl. Judge, Bengaluru.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The Special Land Acquisition Officer, KIADB, Bengaluru has sent this reference under Sections 30 and 31(2) of L.A. Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred as 'L.A. Act' for short) for apportionment of compensation amount.
The final notification was issued on 14.06.2006.
The possession has been taken on L.A.C. No.50/2012 18.11.2011.
The L.A.O. has fixed the compensation of Rs.21,50,000/-.
Muniswamappa was working in Accounts General Office as a peon and was in government service and the family had no ancestral properties.
Narasimhaiah was a tenant and was agriculturist and he was granted the said land and he died on 03.01.1995 and subsequently the said land devolved on his heir that is Ammayyamma.
Narasimhaiah and his brothers were separate and each of the brothers had their own property and there was no joint family of any kind whatsoever.
As abundant caution Narasimhaiah and his brothers have entered into Family partition dated 31.03.1975 and the properties whichever items stood in the respective names of the respective brothers were taken and allotted to them and in any event, there was complete severance of status even prior thereto and there was no communion of interest of any kind as between late. Narasimhaiah and his brothers and sisters that is the other respondents.
Hence, prayed to release the entire amount to claimant No. 1.
.7.
The LRs of claimant No. 2 have filed claim statement stating that the present compensation awarded / solatium cannot be disbursed because, suit in O.S.No. 2062/1990 came to be partly decreed and appeal is preferred over the said judgment and decree in RFA No. 1391/2013.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
5 Ammayyamma was managing the affairs of the joint family as a kartha and he was purchased /
acquired the same from and out of the joint family funds and after his death the said property was transferred in the name of his wife Ammayyamma i.e., claimant No. 1.
The joint family was carrying on milk vending business since several decades and had very good income.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is held that the plaintiff is entitled to partition and separate possession of his 1/8th share in item No. 1 and 2 of schedule 'A' property, the ) Ammayyamma vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 15 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167841535/
7 defendants 1(a) to 1(j) L.A.C. No.50/2012 together entitled to 1/8th share and the defendants 3(a) to 3(d) are together entitled to 1/8th share and defendants 2, 4 and 7 are entitled to 1/8th share each in item No. 1 and 9 of the suit schedule 'A' property.
The suit of the plaintiff in-respect of suit schedule 'B' property is dismissed.
PW.1 has stated that other claimants have no right or share in the compensation amount and the claimant No. 1 is alone entitled to receive the compensation amount.
From the oral and documentary evidence, it is clear that Narasimhaiah has been granted the land by the Land Tribunal.
From the judgment in Ex.P.2, it is clear that the acquired property bearing Sy.No. 14 is self acquired property of Narasimhaiah.
The said Narasimhaiah died and his legal heirs have contended that the compensation amount can be paid to the claimant No. 1 Ammayyamma.
During the pendency of the case, Ammayyamma has expired.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Accordingly point No.1 is answered partly in the affirmative.
.26. Point No.2:
The reference made by the respondent/SLAO, KIADB, Bengaluru under Sections 30 and 31(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 is hereby partly allowed.
LRs of Claimant No. 1 are entitled to receive the compensation amount in guntas of Hosakerehalli village, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluka with accrued interest thereon, subject to the result in RFA No.1391/2013 C/w RFA COB L.A.C.
No.50/2012 33/2013, which is pending on the file of the Hon'ble High Court.
The parties are at liberty to seek for modification of the order in terms of judgment in RFA No. 1391/2013 and connected case.
The above claimants shall have to execute indemnity bond with one surety,
undertaking to re-deposit the compensation amount either in this court or in any other court, if ordered to do so, which amount they are going to receive in this case.
The reference made by the respondent in-respect of claimant No. 2 is dismissed.
The reference made by the respondent in-respect of claimant No. 3 to 8 is rejected.
Draw award accordingly.
